title: nearby-fauna.csv distances are kilometres labelled as miles
description:
tools/fetch-nearby-fauna.mjs:132 passes RADII_MI straight to the iNaturalist species_counts 'radius' param. That param is in KM, not miles — tools/fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs:317 already knows this and multiplies by MI_TO_KM.

Verified live against the backyard coordinates (2026-09-13), Aves:
  radius=3      -> 166 species
  radius=4.828  -> 330 species   (3 mi expressed in km)

So every 'nearest_radius_mi' value in ecology/nearby-fauna.csv is really a kilometre figure: the '3 mi' band actually covered 1.86 mi, and each band holds roughly half the species it should.

Two consequences:
1. src/analysis/faunaMatches.js RANGE_THRESHOLD_MI compares miles against kilometres, so inRange is wrong.
2. Anything rendering 'confirmed within N mi' overstates the distance.

Fix: convert in fetch-nearby-fauna.mjs the same way fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs does, then re-fetch. Found while adding establishment_means to the same file.
close_reason: Closed

title: Un-pin / condense the sticky toolbar on mobile
description:
styles.css:56 sets .view-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0 }. Measured 547px tall at 412px wide = 60% of a 915px viewport and ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. Confirmed pinning at top:0 across scrollY 400-1200, i.e. the entire range where any view is on screen. Usable height below it is 368px measured, ~233px on device - less than the 278px height of a single .view. The app's only content cannot fit on screen.

It stacks, vertically, at 412px: legend (3 items), 5 layer chips wrapping to 3 ragged right-aligned rows (105px), 2 pill switches + Undo/Redo, month label+slider+readout, scale label+slider+number input, and a 3-bar 'Scale reference' card with a hint line.
design:
Options:
- Drop position:sticky below ~960px, or keep only a ~56px condensed bar (month scrubber + a 'Controls' button) pinned and move the rest into a bottom sheet / <details> drawer.
- The month slider is the core interaction and the one control worth permanent space. Scale, layers, labels, lock, undo/redo and the legend are set-once-then-forget.
- Move the legend and 'Scale reference' card below the views or into the drawer.
- Collapse the scale row: #scaleInput duplicates #scaleSlider, and each view already renders its own '1 ft = N px' badge (.view-scale).
acceptance_criteria: At 412x915, a complete .view is visible on screen at the same time as whatever toolbar remains pinned.
close_reason: view-toolbar drops position:sticky below 960px, verified in 412x915 iframe

title: Tap a plant to open a species detail sheet
description:
On mobile there is no way to see species details by touch. Provable from source; a resized desktop browser has hover and will falsely appear to work.

- Details are delivered ONLY through native SVG <title> tooltips (src/render/tooltip.js -> renderTopView / renderElevationView). Confirmed 192 <title> elements for 192 plant groups. <title> never fires on touch.
- styles.css reinforces this with '.view svg [data-name]:hover { cursor: pointer }'.
- Species table cross-highlighting is bound to mouseenter/mouseleave (src/app.js:734-735) - hover-only.
- Clone is bound to contextmenu (src/app.js:522), and a document click handler at :541 hides the menu. Android long-press over SVG should be verified on-device rather than assumed, but there is no discoverable tap affordance either way.

Net: tapping a plant on a phone does nothing. The species table at the bottom of a 7-screen page is the only route to details and is disconnected from the plant you tapped.
design:
Add a click/pointerup handler on [data-plant-id] that opens a bottom sheet rendering buildTooltipLines(plant, state), plus a 'Clone' action - this reuses the existing tooltip builder and replaces the contextmenu-only clone path with something that works on both input types. Mirror mouseenter/mouseleave on species rows with click-to-pin highlighting. Keep the <title> elements: they remain the desktop tooltip and the accessible name.

Blast radius (codegraph impact buildTooltipLines): tooltip.js, topView.js, elevationViews.js, renderViews.js, tests/topView.test.js, tests/elevationViews.test.js.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a plant in any of the three views opens a detail sheet with the same content the desktop tooltip shows, and offers Clone. No regression to the existing <title> tooltips.
close_reason: tap [data-plant-id] opens a bottom detail sheet (buildTooltipLines content) with a Clone action; verified via headless iframe at 412x915, existing SVG <title> tooltips unaffected

title: touch-action:none while unlocked swallows page scroll over every view
description:
src/interaction/dragController.js:170 and :349 set svg.style.touchAction = locked ? 'auto' : 'none'. Verified: with positions unlocked, all three view SVGs compute touch-action:none.

Each view is 370x278 inside a 412px column, so any vertical swipe that STARTS on a drawing is swallowed and the page will not scroll. With three views stacked, most of the scrollable area is dead. This is the single most maddening mobile behavior in the app, and is half the reason the scrolling feels 'nested'.

Locked is the default (lockToggle checked, no localStorage on first visit), so a first-time visitor will not hit this - but it makes editing on a phone effectively impossible.
design:
Either:
- use touch-action: pan-y instead of none while unlocked, so vertical page scroll survives and drags read as horizontal/hold gestures; or
- require a long-press (or tap-to-select-then-drag) to begin a touch drag, keeping touch-action:auto until that gesture is recognized.

Blast radius (codegraph impact createPlantDragController): dragController.js, src/app.js init.
acceptance_criteria: With positions unlocked on a touch device, a vertical swipe starting on a drawing scrolls the page, and dragging a plant still works.
close_reason: touch-action: pan-y instead of none, preserves vertical page scroll while unlocked

title: app.db foundation: open-once connection, migration runner, users table
description: Several beads need data/app.db and assumed someone else would create it: identity needs users, the yard move needs projects and revisions, saved areas need owner_id. This bead creates it first. Scope: a server/db module that opens data/app.db once when the server starts, with WAL, foreign_keys=ON and busy_timeout=5000, and passes the handle through ctx; a small numbered-migration runner (a schema_version table, one migration file per change); and migration 001: users(id, email UNIQUE, is_admin, created_at). The owner is seeded from an OWNER_EMAIL env var as the first admin. DATA_DIR is honoured (default data/), and tests and the e2e scratch server get a throwaway app.db. List app.db under Data safety in AGENTS.md as non-rebuildable.

title: History stores placements only; a plant is species + placement
description: Each history entry currently copies full plant objects (colours, months, sizes, preferences), and rehydratePlants then discards those attributes and rebuilds them from the catalog. As a result history is 10-20x larger than needed (example-frontyard: 297 entries, 5.5 MB), and historyMatchesLayout finds the matching entry by turning every entry back into CSV and comparing the text. Change: a placement is {id, speciesId, x, y, status, source} (status and source come from the lifecycle bead); displayed plants are always built as createPlantFromSpecies(species, placement). The history_entries table in app.db stores placements only; planting_layout.csv becomes an export; historyMatchesLayout and findHistoryEntryIndexByLayout go away.
acceptance_criteria: A history entry contains no species attributes; undo after a catalog change shows the current catalog values; the migrated history keeps every entry.

title: Revision history for yard setup and features, not just plantings
description: project.json (views, site, yard size) and features.json (house, beds, fences) are overwritten on each save with no history; the route comments already warn that 'there is no history to recover it from'. With other people editing yards the owner cannot repair by hand, that is not acceptable. Change: in app.db, every save of the setup, the features, or the planting creates a revision that shares one revision number per project, so undo/redo and history can step across all three. Store the full setup/features JSON for each revision (it is small), and placements as in the placements bead.

title: Reference species by stable id everywhere, not by botanical name
description: A layout row today is id,botanical_name,x_ft,y_ft. buildPlantsFromCsv finds the species by the normalized botanical name, and if that fails it falls back to the species epithet alone. A botanical rename (ecology/fnct-name-changes.csv exists because names change) turns saved yards into 'Unknown plant', or the epithet fallback matches the wrong species. plants.csv already has a stable slug id that layouts ignore, and the claim store's taxa table has resolves_to for synonyms but no slug id. Change: plants.csv id becomes the only species key in layouts, history, rules and exports. Add a taxon_id column that links it to claims taxa, route any name matching (imports, CSV) through taxa.resolves_to, and drop the epithet-only fallback. Migrate the existing layouts and history. Do this before nl-3s5.3, so other users' data is born with the stable key.
acceptance_criteria: Renaming a species' botanical_name in plants.csv leaves every saved yard rendering the same plants; no code path finds a species by epithet alone.

title: Reject cross-site requests on POST, PUT and DELETE
description: collectPayload parses any body as JSON, whatever its Content-Type, so a text/plain POST from another site gets past it. Once users are logged in, that lets a malicious page send requests using their session. On every state-changing request, require Content-Type: application/json (the background upload keeps its own image type check), and require that the Origin header matches the site's hostname. This does not depend on how the Access login cookie is configured.

title: Request helpers: requireUser, loadOwnedProject, json(), rate limiter
description: Every route repeats its own try/catch and writes its own response. Before auth is added route by route, add helpers to server/http.js: requireUser(ctx), loadOwnedProject(ctx), which returns 404 for a yard that doesn't exist or isn't the caller's, json(res, status, body), and a per-user token-bucket rate limiter. With these, the ownership rule is tested once instead of on each of ten routes. No framework.

title: Deploy from a pinned commit, not the live working tree
description: docker-compose bind-mounts the repo at /app, so the working tree IS production, and every half-finished edit (by a person or an agent) reaches users immediately. Before anyone else uses the site, run production from a separate checkout (a git worktree on a deploy branch) or an image built from a commit, with only DATA_DIR mounted. The e2e scratch server and local development keep the bind mount. Rewrite AGENTS.md's 'test, commit, restart' so it deploys deliberately, and update the checks for a verified restart. The cloudflared service and its 'web' service name must not change.
notes: Owner decision 2026-09-23: use a git worktree (for example ../native_landscaping-deploy, detached at a main commit) as the live site; web and feed-poller bind-mount it instead of the dev tree. Deploys must happen AUTOMATICALLY once a change lands on main. Put the hooks in a tracked directory (core.hooksPath=.githooks, set by an npm run setup or a documented one-liner). post-commit and post-merge fire only when the branch is main (a fast-forward merge fires post-merge, not post-commit) and run tools/deploy.sh. deploy.sh: in the deploy worktree, git checkout --detach main; docker compose restart web (and feed-poller if tools/feedState/ or fetch-observation-events changed); then verify that StartedAt changed and that a request for a changed file serves the new content; if it fails, stop loudly and do NOT roll forward half-way. Commits on agent worktree branches never deploy. data/ must stay one shared directory (DATA_DIR pointed at the dev tree's data/ or a path outside both trees), NOT a copy in each worktree. Update AGENTS.md's 'test, commit, restart' section to say that a commit to main deploys itself, and how to check that the deploy happened.

title: Off-machine backups of app.db and user photos
description: Other people's yards will be data that cannot be rebuilt. Take a nightly consistent snapshot (sqlite3 .backup or VACUUM INTO) of app.db plus the photos under DATA_DIR, copy it off the machine, and keep several versions; alternatively, Litestream continuous replication. Document the restore steps in AGENTS.md and do one test restore.
acceptance_criteria: A documented restore from last night's backup has been done once, successfully.
notes:
Owner input needed: where the off-machine copies go (for example B2/S3 or another machine).
Owner decision 2026-09-23: store backups on Google Drive using rclone. The owner creates the Drive remote once, interactively (rclone config, Google OAuth). Put an rclone 'crypt' remote on top of it: backups hold other users' yards and possibly locations, so Drive must only ever see ciphertext; the crypt password stays in a gitignored file, and the owner also keeps it offline, because losing it makes the backups useless. Nightly job (a compose service or host cron): sqlite3 VACUUM INTO a snapshot of app.db, plus the photos under DATA_DIR, into a dated folder, then rclone copy to the crypt remote; keep 14 dailies and 8 weeklies. The restore steps go in AGENTS.md, and one test restore must be done.

title: Move saved areas and feed state into app.db
description: Move the hand-entered saved_areas and feed_state tables from saved-areas.db and feed-state.db into data/app.db, so owner_id can be a real foreign key to users and there is one file to back up. The caches (ecosystem, claims, probe-cache, observation-events) stay separate and rebuildable. Retire data/saved-areas.export.json once backups (the backups bead) cover it: it is a committed snapshot, and with more than one user it would carry other people's area names. Update AGENTS.md's Data safety section.

title: Authorize every project route by owner
description: Check ownership on every ?project= route: GET /api/history, POST /api/layout, /api/project, /api/projects (create in the caller's own namespace), GET/POST /api/features, /api/history/cursor, /api/view-background, the new image GET route, and GET /api/ecosystem, which today returns any project's lat/lng from location.json. Return 404, not 403, for a project the caller doesn't own, so ids aren't disclosed. Store a visibility field on project.json, default 'private', so the future public-view work (see the deferred child) has a place to hang without a migration.
acceptance_criteria: A test proves that user A gets 404 on every route for user B's project.
notes: Revised 2026-09-23: the read-only example yard is nl-3s5.24. This bead covers owner checks only.

title: Identity: verify the Cloudflare Access JWT and attach req.user
description: Read Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion and verify its signature, audience and expiry against the team's certs. Do not trust Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email on its own: feed-poller and anything else on the host can reach web:8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080 and forge the header. Fetching and caching the certs is a third-party call, so it lives in tools/. Add a small users table (email, created_at, is_admin) in a new, non-rebuildable data/users.db, and list it under Data safety in AGENTS.md. Provide an explicit dev/test identity (an env flag, off by default) so npm test and the scratch e2e server keep working.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover a valid token, a bad signature, the wrong audience, an expired token, and a forged email header with no JWT; routes receive ctx.user.
notes: Revised 2026-09-23: the users table lives in app.db, created by nl-3s5.23, not in a separate users.db. This no longer waits on nl-3s5.1. Owner input needed: the Access team domain and the application AUD tag.

title: Move user data into data/app.db (SQLite) and out of git and the served root
description: Today projects/* (project.json, features.json, layouts, history, and the yard photos in img/) is tracked in a PUBLIC repo, and it is stored as files that are updated by read-modify-write. Replace that with one gitignored, non-rebuildable data/app.db, opened once when the server starts, with foreign_keys=ON and busy_timeout set. Tables: users (from nl-3s5.2), projects (id, owner_id, slug unique per owner, name, visibility default 'private', config_json, features_json, updated_at), history_entries (project_id, seq, description, plants_json, created_at) plus a cursor on projects. Each save is one transaction, so there are no torn writes and no lost updates between two tabs. Photos go on disk under DATA_DIR/<ownerId>/<projectId>/img, outside the served root, and are served through an authorized GET route. planting_layout.csv becomes an export, not the stored copy. Migration: import all four existing yards as the owner's, with full history. Seed 'backyard' as a separate READ-ONLY example copy that has no location (see the notes). Afterwards, stop tracking projects/* apart from whatever the example needs. Update resolveProjectPaths callers, server/files.js, the e2e scratch server (which gets its own app.db) and docs/testing.md. List app.db under Data safety in AGENTS.md, and extend the delete-guard hook if needed.
acceptance_criteria: A design session leaves git status clean; saving the same yard from two concurrent requests keeps both history entries; killing the server mid-save never empties the history; npm test and e2e pass.
notes:
Owner decision 2026-09-23: all four existing yards (backyard, example-frontyard, walkway, linh-and-nam-s-backyard) belong to the owner and move into the owner's private DATA_DIR. Only 'backyard' is also shared as the example yard. Every user sees it READ-ONLY, as a copy kept separate from the owner's live yard, with no location.json and no coordinates. The other three stop being tracked going forward. They remain in git history, and the owner has not asked for history to be rewritten.
Revised 2026-09-23: app.db, the users table and the migration runner come from nl-3s5.23. Revisions for yard setup and features (nl-3s5.20) now come AFTER this bead and are built on app.db. Setup and features never had history, so nothing is migrated twice. Migrate history straight into the placement-only shape from nl-3s5.19. The read-only example copy is split out into nl-3s5.24.

title: Multi-user: invited users with private yards
description: Let invited people (Google accounts added to the existing Cloudflare Access policy) use Rewilder with their own yards, saved areas and feed. Decisions (2026-09-23, owner): invited only, no public sign-up; one owner per yard for now; the no-yard pages (Start here, Buy plants, Your rights, Flora index) become public; the site's scope is Dallas and surrounding towns until the data grows. Future work, not in scope here: public yard views with owner-controlled privacy, and regions beyond DFW. Order: close the static-file leak, then identity, then move user data out of git and the served root, then authorization, then per-user feed and ecosystem, then open the public pages and onboard people.
notes: BUILDING WITH PARALLEL SUBAGENTS (2026-09-23). Until nl-3s5.12 lands, the repo's working tree IS the live site (it is bind-mounted into the web container), so every agent works in its own git worktree (Agent isolation: worktree) and never edits the main tree. Only the orchestrator merges into main, runs npm test, commits, restarts web, and runs bd (claim/close/note); worktrees don't carry the gitignored Dolt DB. One bead per agent. Lanes that can run at once, because they touch different files: (A) server/static.js leak fix nl-3s5.1; (B) app.db foundation, then identity, then request helpers, in server/db + server/http.js; (C) domain model nl-3s5.18 then .19 in src/data, src/state and plants.csv; (D) deploy nl-3s5.12 in docker-compose and AGENTS.md; (E) nl-3s5.14 in tools/*Db.js and the routes. Do not run two agents that both edit server/routes/*.js or src/data/plantParser.js at the same time.

title: Rarity lane skeleton: local-scarcity fact + filter toggle plumbing
description:
Pure src/analysis/rarity.js classifier + tools/feedState/ loader + feed.js 'rarity' branch + #laneFilter option + describeRelevance() branch, matching the invasive-monitor/yard-relevance lane pattern (tools/feedState/feed.js).

Fact source: species_observations.observation_count from data/ecosystem.db (tools/ecosystemIndexDb.js), joined by taxon against the area's resolved 'place' (server-side, like ecoregion is resolved in server.js:441-449 for yard-relevance). Missing/stale ecosystem.db must produce a warning (ok:false/reason bail-out pattern from yardRelevanceTables.js), never be treated as 'zero observations = rare'.

Scarcity threshold and inclusion criteria are user-supplied filter query params on /api/feed (like unreadOnly/includeDismissed), computed server-side BEFORE queryFeed's pagination/total — never client-side filtering in feedPage.js, and never a synthesized rarity score/label. Sort stays observed_on DESC.

Tests: pure classifier unit test (tests/rarity.test.js, mirrors tests/invasiveWatchlist.test.js) + lane integration test in tests/feed.test.js mirroring the yard-relevance/invasive-monitor cases including the missing-ecosystem.db warning case.
close_reason: Implemented: src/analysis/rarity.js pure classifier, tools/feedState/rarityTables.js loader against ecosystem.db's species_counts, feed.js 'rarity' lane branch, /api/feed rarity_threshold + server-resolved place plumbing, feed.html/feedPage.js UI (lane option, place editor, threshold filter, fact rendering). 9 new tests pass (5 classifier unit, 4 lane integration incl. missing-place and missing-index warnings). Committed 06a9383, deployed (docker compose restart web verified via StartedAt/Pid + served bytes).

title: Feed UI shell
description: New page (or new mode on an existing page) rendering /api/feed items as a list with mark-read controls and per-area filter/tuning controls. Ship this against a trivial 'all new observations in area X' feed first to validate the whole pipeline (polling, dedup, read state, UI) before any feature-specific lane is layered on top.
close_reason: feed.html + feed.css + src/feed/feedPage.js: area picker/creator, feed list with mark-read/dismiss, unread-only/show-dismissed filters, load-more pagination. Verified live in browser.

title: Saved-area config
description: Config for monitoring areas independent of yard projects: name, center lat/lng + radius (or polygon later), and per-area filter settings (taxon scope, invasive-only, rarity threshold, yard-relevant genera). Today only one 'place' exists per project (project.json + gitignored location.json), 1:1-ish with a yard — the brainstormed features explicitly want monitoring of arbitrary areas, so this can't just reuse the project model.
design: Simplest shape: a new JSON file or SQLite table (saved_areas: id, name, lat, lng, radius_mi, filters_json). No auth/multi-user in this app, so a single flat list is fine — no per-user scoping needed.
close_reason: Merged 06e7ef8. SQLite store (tools/savedAreas/savedAreasDb.js) + /api/saved-areas CRUD routes wired into server.js. 13 tests passing.

title: Feed read/unread state + /api/feed routes
description: Server-side SQLite flags (observation_id, read, dismissed) plus GET /api/feed (paginated, filterable, joined with read state) and POST endpoints to mark read/unread/dismissed. Confirmed no existing read/unread/seen/dismiss pattern anywhere in the codebase (grepped client and server) — this is net-new. Server-side chosen over localStorage since this is a single-user local app with no auth and state should be consistent across devices/browsers.

title: Observation event log + incremental fetch script

design: Reuse from fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs: per-taxon radius bands, captive=false/quality_grade=research/taxon_geoprivacy=open/geoprivacy=open filters, ~1.5s request delay. Reuse probeCache.js's (source,endpoint,cache_key) pattern for raw response caching if helpful, though the incremental id_above/updated_since query shape means most of the value is in NOT re-fetching, not in caching what's fetched. description: Shared prerequisite for all three feature lanes (yard-relevance, invasive monitor, rarity/discovery): turn iNaturalist data from a species-presence snapshot into an event log of individual, timestamped, dismissible feed items. Staged so a thin vertical slice (any area, any taxon, all-new-observations) proves the pipeline end-to-end before feature-specific logic is layered on.
design: Stage 1-4 below, roughly in dependency order but 2 and 3 can run in parallel once 1 lands. Ship a trivial 'all new observations in area X' feed after stage 4 to validate polling/dedup/UI before starting the feature lanes.
close_reason: All 4 children merged and verified: observation event log + incremental poller (5218427), saved-area config (06e7ef8), feed read/unread state + /api/feed routes, feed.html UI shell verified live in browser. title: iNaturalist power tool: observation feed (invasive / rarity / yard-relevance)
description: A tunable web feed of iNaturalist observations for saved areas, with per-item read/unread state, replacing the email/report framing from initial brainstorm with an in-app feed per the owner's stated UX preference. Three feature lanes on top of shared foundational infrastructure: invasive species monitoring, rarity/discovery, and yard-relevance (missing keystone genera / associated fauna spotted nearby).
design:
See survey findings (2026-09-20 session): existing data/ecosystem.db (built by nl-a7e) is a species-presence SNAPSHOT (one row per place+taxon, replaced on each manual run), not an event log — no observation IDs, no per-observation timestamps, no diff/history. All three feature lanes need individual timestamped dismissible items, so a foundational event log + incremental poller is a hard prerequisite, not something any one lane can skip.

API feasibility confirmed: iNaturalist recommends ~1 req/sec, 60/min, ~10K/day; id_above/updated_since support incremental fetch. At personal scale (a few saved areas, polled every 15-60 min) this is nowhere near the ceiling — not a constraint on design.

Reuse: tools/fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs's existing per-taxon radius bands, captive/quality/geoprivacy filtering, and probeCache.js's (source,endpoint,cache_key) response cache are all directly reusable patterns for the new incremental fetch script. establishmentMeans.js already captures introduced/naturalized/invasive on every fetched row (just filtered out at the /api/ecosystem route, not at fetch time) — invasive-monitor data mostly already exists. plantMatches.js's host-genera.csv / plant-animal-interactions.csv join is the yard-relevance logic already built, just needs to run against events instead of a snapshot.

Hard boundary carried over from nl-3hi (owner's explicit stance, applies here too): no invented composite scores. Rarity/relevance must be shown as facts (observation counts, distance bands, dates) the same way plantMatches.js already avoids inventing a score from iNaturalist observation_count. This directly affects the rarity lane's design and is why it's sequenced last, pending a rarity-definition decision from the owner.
close_reason: All four children complete: foundational event log, invasive-monitor, yard-relevance, and rarity/discovery feed lanes are shipped.

title: Flora corpus .txt dumps are committed to a public repo, against the project's own rule
description:
git ls-files docs/data-acquisition/corpus/ returns all six FNCT_*.txt extractions (~65,000 lines of the 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas). They are tracked and public.

This contradicts a rule the project wrote for itself. docs/data-acquisition/03-document-corpus.md section 2, under 'Licensing: fact extraction only': 'the PDFs and every text dump stay in the scratchpad and out of the repo -- they are 100 MB of copyrighted text, and committing them would be both bloat and a licensing problem.' .gitignore excludes docs/data-acquisition/corpus/*.pdf and stops there; corpus/NOTICE.md makes the same free-to-download-not-free-to-redistribute point the .txt files violate.

The PDFs are correctly excluded, so the intent is clearly recorded -- only the extension in the ignore pattern is wrong.

Found while scoping nl-scx (the data-acquisition implementation epic). Filed separately rather than folded in: it is a licensing exposure on a public repo, not implementation work, and should not wait on that epic.
design:
Two parts, and the second is the one that takes thought.

1. Widen the .gitignore pattern to cover the extractions as well as the PDFs.
2. Decide whether removing them from the CURRENT tree is enough, or whether history needs rewriting. The repo is public, so the text is already published and reachable through history. A history rewrite is destructive and force-pushes to a public branch -- do NOT do it without asking the owner first.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: several nl-41o docs cite corpus line numbers as evidence (e.g. 06 section 2 cites corpus/FNCT_0210-0617-Acanth-Euph.txt:5047-5052 for the Aster oblongifolius bracket crosswalk, and lines 5043/5111/5119/5127 for the glued-genus hazard), and nl-scx.3 and nl-scx.4 both build against that corpus. Removing the files from the working tree would break reproducibility for whoever picks those up. They need a documented local path -- regenerate with pdftotext -layout from the PDFs, which 03 section 2 confirms are freely downloadable from the Austin College page.
acceptance_criteria:
- .gitignore excludes the .txt extractions as well as the PDFs
- The tracked .txt files are removed from the working tree
- A documented way to regenerate them locally exists, so the doc citations stay checkable
- A decision on history rewrite is recorded, made by the repo owner, not assumed

comments.author: John Syrinek
comments.text: Resolved as won't-fix per owner decision 2026-09-20: the corpus .txt extractions are reasonable use since they are not the copyrighted PDFs themselves, and the PDFs are freely downloadable from BRIT (Austin College page cited in docs/data-acquisition/03-document-corpus.md). No history rewrite, no gitignore change, no working-tree removal needed. History-rewrite question was asked and explicitly declined.

title: Export generator: plants.csv as a projection of the claim store
description: Generate plants.csv from the store instead of hand-editing it. 04 section 4 decided to keep the flat CSV rather than teach the app SQLite: plantParser.js and everything downstream expects flat rows, and 'git diff plants.csv' stays a two-line change a human can read where a claims.db diff would be binary noise.
design:
Implements 04 section 4 (the four steps) and 04 section 4.1 (the newline rule).

Four steps, in order: (1) resolve each (species, field) through nl-scx.5's precedence rule; (2) keep ONLY status='asserted' -- review and unknown rows are excluded entirely; (3) evaluate the resolved claim's license grant against the project's CURRENT commercial status; (4) walk cultivar inheritance per 04 section 2.3 -- own claim first, else the parent species' -- before applying the same two filters.

STEP 3 NEEDS AN INPUT THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: the project's commercial status. 04 section 3.2 deliberately models license as a GRANT evaluated at export time rather than a boolean baked in at extraction, because LBJ/NPIN's permission is conditional on this project's business model ('personal/non-commercial: yes; commercial: no', the 2026-08-28 reply in permission-requests.md). Today the answer is non-commercial, so NPIN claims pass. Add that one line of project config and read it here -- a claim whose grant is voided drops from the EXPORT, never from the store.

NO EMBEDDED NEWLINES (04 section 4.1): csvLoader.js's parseCsv splits on newlines before honoring quotes, so it cannot represent one. Forbidding at the generator -- the single point -- was chosen over fixing a parser every view depends on for a benefit no current data needs. Replace \n with a space AND LOG when it happens, so a truncated value is visible in the generator's output rather than silently mangled in the CSV.

nl-c58 is closed, which is what makes step 2 safe: an excluded field now reads as a genuine blank downstream instead of becoming 'mound', 1, or a skipped rule-8 check.
acceptance_criteria:
- plants.csv is generated, and regenerating it with no store changes produces a byte-identical file
- A review-status field lands as an empty cell and the app renders it as not-declared, not as a default
- Commercial status is read from config; flipping it to commercial drops NPIN-sourced values from the export and leaves the claims in the store
- Every newline replacement is logged
close_reason: Built tools/claims/exportPlantsCsv.js (04 §4's four steps + §4.1 newline/quote scrub, logged) and tools/claims/projectConfig.js (COMMERCIAL_STATUS, the one line of config §4 step 3 needed). Tests in tests/exportPlantsCsv.test.js: determinism, precedence resolution, review/unknown blanking, commercial-status flip (claim stays in store, drops from export), fail-open on no license row, cultivar inheritance incl. 'own claim that itself blanks does not fall through to parent', newline/quote scrub+log. npm test passes (all suites). NOT run against the live plants.csv: width_ft/foliage_color_spring/fall/winter/inflorescence/flower_count_hint/flower_zone have no claim source yet (usdaIngest.js PLACEHOLDER_KEYS), so a real export today would blank currently-curated values. 'byte-identical on rerun' read as determinism, not 'matches today's hand-edited file'. Also: taxa has no common_name/slug id, so identity (id/common_name/botanical_name + row set) comes from an input identity list defaulting to plants.csv, not invented -- widening identity into the store is a separate bead. Committed 753f925; docker compose restart web verified via StartedAt/Pid change.

title: manual-corrections.tsv: the committed system of record, and its replay
description: Create the file 09 section 2 specifies and the replay step that turns it into claim rows. This file, not a row in claims.db, is authoritative: claims.db is gitignored and rebuildable, and a correction is precisely the class of claim with no source to rebuild from (04 section 3.4). The database row is only ever a projection of it, symmetric with how plants.csv is a projection.
design:
Implements 09 sections 2, 2.1, 5; 04 section 3.4.

PATH: manual-corrections.tsv at the REPO ROOT, alongside plants.csv and the other flat catalogs -- not under docs/data-acquisition/ (design docs, not data) and not under data/ (gitignored store).

TSV, not CSV: 04 section 4.1 already forbids embedded newlines in generated output, and a correction's hand-written reason is the value most likely to contain a comma. TSV avoids quoting that field at all. Every reason is one physical line, no exceptions.

COLUMNS: usda_symbol, field, value, reason, author, date, supersedes_source. usda_symbol rather than taxa.id -- a surrogate key is meaningless in a diff and churns across a rebuild. A cultivar correction keys on symbol + cultivar name (ILVO 'Nana'). reason and author are REQUIRED; the replay step must REJECT a row missing either rather than import it as an unattributed edit. No foreign key into claims.db -- the file has to stay meaningful if the database is deleted.

REPLAY (09 section 2.1) runs LAST, after every sourced claim, and its ordering AC lives on nl-scx.1 where the harness is built. Each row inserts a claim with source='manual-correction', status='asserted', citation=reason, and superseded_by set on the claim it targets. A manual correction outranks every source in the precedence table by construction.

SEED DATA, ready to write and not a design decision (09 section 1.2, from 03 section 7.1's per-taxon review): 7 confirmed-non-native-to-NCTX corrections -- Chilopsis linearis, Catalpa speciosa, Robinia pseudoacacia, Eschscholzia californica, Gymnocladus dioicus, Taxodium distichum, Tillandsia usneoides. Plus 4 review entries: Pinus echinata and Pinus taeda (marginal, the flora declines to say), Cyperus esculentus and Nymphaea mexicana (the flora cites conflicting origins). Six species are confirmed NON-defects and must not be reopened: Quercus muehlenbergii, Maclura pomifera, Heliotropium curassavicum, Impatiens capensis, Phragmites australis, Stachys tenuifolia.
acceptance_criteria:
- manual-corrections.tsv exists at the repo root, committed, with the 7 seed corrections written in the specified format
- Replay rejects a row missing reason or author
- 09 section 5's demonstration holds: after replay, a fresh USDA re-crawl inserts a new claim row and leaves superseded_by untouched, so claims_provenance shows three rows rather than one silently overwritten value
close_reason: manual-corrections.tsv written with the 7 seed corrections; replay auto-vivifies taxa outside plantable_core so it works end-to-end

title: Per-field precedence rule, and the tie that must not resolve
description:
Implement 09 section 1's precedence as code. It is a lookup against a table 02 section 2 already produced (while inventorying access and licensing, not while designing arbitration), not a new mechanism -- precedence is decided once per field, never computed per claim. No confidence weighting, no newest-wins.

Three later pieces have been holding empty slots for this rule since they were specified: 07 section 3.2's claims_provenance.resolutionReason, 07 section 3.6's claims_dry_run.changed, and 05 section 4's Adjudication metric.
design:
Implements 09 sections 1 and 1.1.

The table: USDA primary for county distribution and the 81 characteristics; NPIN primary for month-precision bloom, light-as-a-set, deer resistance, species-level larval host, soil/water description, falling back to USDA's coarser ordinal; NWF primary for genus-level keystone counts; the flora primary for nativity_nctx, falling back to USDA's continental L48:N; iNaturalist NOT admissible as a value source at all (02 section 2.4 -- wild:captive ratio measures a different question and cannot be thresholded into nativity).

WHY PER-FIELD RATHER THAN A FIXED SOURCE RANKING: a fixed ranking ('USDA always beats NPIN') gets Passiflora lutea's sun_pref wrong -- NPIN wins there specifically, and 08 section 1.2 is that correction already made by hand before the rule had a name. Confidence weighting would need a number neither USDA nor the flora publishes, which is the invented-weight move 05 section 1.1 already rejected.

THE TIE THAT MUST NOT AUTO-RESOLVE (09 section 1.1). Two asserted claims disagreeing from sources TIED under the table -- including two literature citations inside one API source -- route to status='review' and stop. No value exports until a human adjudicates. Three real instances are already sitting in the queue: Callicarpa americana's LargeMammals (USDA's own PlantWildlife exposes Martin='Minor' against Miller='Moderate' without ranking them), and inside the flora's own text, Cyperus esculentus (Mabberley 1987 against Tucker 1994) and Nymphaea mexicana (the flora flags its one NCTX record as 'probably a hybrid', undermining its own citation). Picking one by majority, first-seen or alphabetical manufactures a certainty an ecologist reading both papers would not have.
acceptance_criteria:
- Resolving a (species, field) with claims from differently-ranked sources returns the primary's value and a stated reason
- Resolving a tie returns no value and marks the pair for review
- Passiflora lutea's sun_pref resolves to NPIN's value, reproducing commit 1fa2a13's hand-applied correction
- The three known tie cases above land in review, not in an export
close_reason: resolveField implemented and tested per 09 §1/§1.1 AC

title: Flora extraction: NCTX nativity into claims, with page citations
description: Extract nativity from the NCTX flora corpus into claim rows. The flora is PRIMARY for nativity_nctx and outranks USDA's continental L48:N at NCTX scale (09 section 1) -- this is the ingest that closes the epic's founding gap, that continental nativity scores desert willow and Mexican plum identically.
design:
Implements 03 sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; consumes nl-scx.3's mapping.

pdftotext -layout is sufficient; no OCR, no Python (03 section 2 -- real embedded text). CITATION IS EXACT: pdftotext emits one form-feed per page and page = first_page_in_filename + formfeed_index, verified with zero drift on three volumes. Claims cite e.g. 'Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, p. 771'.

LICENSING IS A HARD CONSTRAINT ON WHAT GETS STORED (03 section 2): extract VALUES plus a page citation, never excerpts. A nativity flag is a fact; the prose is expression.

THREE-VALUED, not two (03 sections 4, 5):
- The I symbol is reliable -> asserted introduced
- A prose origin statement is a SCREEN, never an auto-assignment -> status='review'. 03 section 4 is explicit: 'prose match => queue for review, never auto-assign'
- No treatment found -> status='unknown'. Collapsing this into native is the exact failure that promotes a non-native into a recommendation
SILENCE DOES NOT IMPLY NATIVE: 03 section 4.1 measured an 11.6% leak on the converse.

The two truncation hazards 03 section 6 already found and fixed must stay fixed in production code: a heading must follow a blank line (a wrapped common name otherwise reads as the next heading), and each span is bounded at the next heading or a REFERENCES: block (a genus synopsis otherwise bleeds into the next taxon). Both were invisible in the output and obvious in the controls -- validate against a labelled control set, same as 06 section 6.
acceptance_criteria:
- Nativity claims exist for every plantable-set species the corpus treats, each carrying a real page citation
- No excerpt of flora prose is written to the store or to any committed file
- The three states are distinct in the store; a prose-origin hit never lands as 'asserted'
- 03 section 7.1's 17 already-reviewed taxa reproduce their recorded verdicts when the extractor runs over them
close_reason:
Implemented in commit ef51fd5 (tools/claims/floraNativity.js + rebuild.js wiring + tests/floraNativity.test.js).

All 15 reconciliation-reachable species from 03 §7.1's 17-taxon review reproduce their recorded page citations exactly and screen to 'review' (never auto-asserted), matching "prose match => queue for review, never auto-assign". Stachys tenuifolia lands as asserted-native via silence rather than review-then-clear — same recorded verdict (native, non-defect), reached more precisely because the span correctly excludes the neighboring key-couplet's phrase 03 §4 already named as a false-positive class. Eschscholzia californica and Taxodium distichum are unreachable: the flora only treats their infraspecific ranks, so nl-scx.3's steps 1/2 leave them matched_via='unmatched' (the steps-3-5 residual, not this bead's scope) — both are independently covered by the already-committed ESCA2/TADI2 manual corrections.

Two origin-phrase hits outside 03 §7.1's table (Anemopsis californica, Elephantopus carolinianus) now surface in the review queue too — expected per 03 §4.1 ("a wider screen surfaces more"), not a regression, noted here so nl-scx.10's conflicts view doesn't read them as new.

Found and fixed a real plantable_core coverage gap while validating AC bullet 1: rebuild.js only reconciled blackland-prairie-natives.csv, so a plants.csv-only species (Silphium albiflorum) got no name_reconciliations row and no nativity_nctx claim at all, not unknown even. Fixed by including plants.csv rows absent from the wider catalog in the reconciliation input.

title: Name reconciliation: catalog name to flora heading
description:
Implement 06 section 3's five-step resolution, which must run BEFORE any flora lookup. Until it does, 'no treatment found' is uninterpretable -- 03 section 5 measured 119 of 469 blackland-prairie-natives.csv rows matching no treatment, and traced the cause to 1999 nomenclature (Symphyotrichum oblongifolium is treated, but only under Aster oblongifolius), not to genuine absence.

Reconciliation produces a name mapping; extraction consumes it. Keeping them separate steps is what makes the mapping reusable by any future book source -- 1999-vs-current naming is a property of any older taxonomic work, not a flora quirk.
design:
Implements 06 sections 3, 4, 5, 6. Writes name_reconciliations rows (built by nl-scx.1) and sets taxa.resolves_to.

MEASUREMENT GATE, and it is an AC not an afterthought (06 section 7, first open item): build step 2 alone -- the flora's OWN bracketed synonym crosswalk, parsed offline as a byproduct of the same header scan -- run it across the 119, and COUNT the residual BEFORE building the network path in steps 3-5. The doc's point is that the USDA round trip may be needed for a far smaller remainder than assumed. Do not build steps 3-5 against an unmeasured assumption.

Two measured hazards the parser must survive:
- GLUED GENUS-SPECIES in bracket citations: Symphyotrichumlateriflorum, Symphyotrichumpratense, Symphyotrichumsericeum, Symphyotrichumdivaricatum all appear with no space (corpus/FNCT_0210-0617-Acanth-Euph.txt lines 5043, 5111, 5119, 5127). A parser assuming 'Genus species' has a space silently drops these.
- RANK-AWARE headers (03 section 6c): a binomial-only regex misses Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica though the flora carries it. Try the infraspecific heading first, fall back to the plain species heading only if no infraspecific heading exists.

A PARTIAL rank match -- species heading present, the variety's own epithet absent -- is status='review' carrying the species-level value as a candidate, never 'asserted' (06 section 4). A variety can carry a range or origin the species text does not speak to, and nothing in the header grammar tells the algorithm which case it is in.

Ambiguous USDA name (alternatives but no exact match): status='review' carrying the alternatives, no guess (06 section 3 step 3).
Reuse search.js's existing binomialOf helper for author-citation stripping rather than writing a second one (06 section 7).
Never run against a taxa row of rank='cultivar' -- no taxonomic work treats a cultivar (06 section 7).
acceptance_criteria:
- 06 section 6's control set passes in BOTH directions, including the glued-genus row and the known true-negatives (Bouvardia ternifolia, Liatris punctata)
- The step-2-only residual against the 119 is measured and recorded before steps 3-5 exist
- 06 section 6's two OPEN control rows (an ambiguous-name instance, an infraspecific partial match) are either filled from the real catalog run or recorded as confirmed-absent
- Every reconciliation writes a name_reconciliations row, including matched_via='unmatched'
close_reason: reconcile() implements 06 §3 steps 1/2/6 + §4's partial-match review; measured residual against blackland-prairie-natives.csv: 327 direct, 12 flora-synonym (7 needing review), 128 unmatched — recorded before steps 3-5 (USDA-synonym network path, left for a future bead). Ambiguous-name control row stays OPEN pending that path; infraspecific partial-match row filled from a real hit (Aristida purpurea var. longiseta).

title: USDA ingest: characteristics and county distribution into claims
description: Turn the existing tools/usda-plants fetch path into claim rows rather than CSV columns. USDA is PRIMARY for county distribution and the 81 characteristics (09 section 1's precedence table), so this is the bulk of the store's content and the first real exercise of the schema.
design:
Implements 04 section 3.1 (citation shape), 04 section 3.2 (license row), 02 section 2.1 (source role), 10 section 2.1 (the county gate).

CITATION for an API-sourced claim is not a page reference: store the endpoint and the id the request used, e.g. usda-plants:PlantCharacteristics:QUSH. 04 section 3.1's rule is that a claim a human or a probe cannot re-derive is an assertion, not a claim.

LICENSE row: grant=unrestricted, condition=NULL (02 section 2.1 -- public domain, cleanest terms here).

COUNTY PRESENCE is the gate, not a ranking signal (10 section 2.1). 01 section 3.1 measured it available at the needed granularity for every species tried -- this is the one layer of the plantable set that is complete.

DO NOT gate any USDA call on the lightweight search endpoint's HasCharacteristics / HasSynonyms booleans: 06 section 2 measured both as unpopulated regardless of the true answer (PlantSynonyms/40799 returns 7 records while HasSynonyms reads false). Call the dedicated endpoints directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every species in the plantable set has USDA-sourced claims in the store, each with source, citation, retrieved_at and license_id populated
- Re-running the ingest inserts new claim rows and never UPDATEs or deletes an existing one (04 section 3.1)
- A species USDA has no characteristics record for produces status='unknown' claims, not missing rows and not fabricated values -- the ~2,200-species coverage limit nl-9a6 measured is a real answer, recorded as one
close_reason: Merged into main. Real end-to-end run against live USDA API: 4140 claims (3531 characteristics, 99 county), plantable_set narrowed 102->73 once the Dallas Co. county gate went live. 63 species with a characteristics record, 32 status=unknown, 4 unresolved-by-name (also unknown), 3 cultivars correctly skipped. Pure-insert re-run verified. tests/usdaIngest.test.js: 9 tests, npm test passes (all suites).

comments.author: John Syrinek
comments.text: nl-yud (unblocking this bead) added 9 new raw usda_* columns (Commercial Availability, Toxicity, Lifespan, Vegetative/Seed Spread Rate, Resprout Ability, Fruit/Seed Persistence, Growth Rate, Height at 20yr Max) and corresponding probe.js target fields, but sampled only on Quercus shumardii. Nothing may assert claims from these 9 fields until a broad-population probe run (across the plantable set) confirms they're actually filled, not mostly-empty. Also fixed water_pref to read Moisture Use only (Drought Tolerance is a different scale, lower bound vs optimum — the old || fallback could invert the answer); Drought Tolerance still lands as its own claim, separate from water_pref.

title: Claim store: schema, rebuild harness, and the plantable set
description:
Create data/claims.db and the rebuild entry point everything else ingests through. Nothing else in this epic can start without it -- 07 section 3 held all six Phase 2 tools back for exactly this reason.

Tables, per 04: taxa (section 2.2 -- resolves_to for synonyms, parent_id for rank/cultivars), claims (section 3.1 -- one row per species/field/source, nothing overwritten on ingest), licenses (section 3.2 -- grant + condition + citation_required, modelled as a grant evaluated later, never a boolean baked in at extraction), name_reconciliations (06 section 5 -- one row per taxa_id+corpus, matched_via, reviewed).

Indexes: (species_id, field), field, source, status -- the four 04 section 5 names as sufficient for all six lookups.
design:
Implements 04 sections 2, 3, 5; 06 section 5; 09 section 2.1; 10 section 2.2.

REBUILD ORDERING IS AN AC HERE, NOT ON THE CORRECTIONS CHILD. 09 section 2.1: the manual-corrections file is replayed LAST, after all sourced claims. Replay-last -- not the append-only claims table by itself -- is what stops a fresh crawl re-claiming the top of the precedence order and silently undoing a correction. A harness built without that ordering is a harness that has to be rebuilt.

THE PLANTABLE SET HAS TO BE MATERIALIZED SOMEWHERE, and this is that place. 05 section 4's per-field completeness query has a literal <plantable set, nl-41o.7> hole in its denominator, and 10 section 2.2's 101 species (plants.csv UNION npsot_dfw_recommended=yes, measured 2026-09-18) is a derivation, not a stored artifact. Materialize it as a view or derivation step, gated by 10 section 2.1's USDA county-presence check for Dallas Co. (FIPS 48113) and screened against the exclusion list, so the metrics and the stopping condition have a real denominator to divide by.

The residual claim about a species in that set is 'not known to be non-native to NCTX', never 'confirmed native' (10 section 2.1). Whatever names the set should not imply otherwise.
acceptance_criteria:
- data/claims.db created via node:sqlite in WAL mode, gitignored (already covered by .gitignore's *.db)
- The four tables and four indexes above exist
- A rebuild entry point drops and repopulates the store from scratch, with corrections replayed as the final step
- The plantable set is queryable, derived not hand-listed, and reproduces 10 section 2.2's measured 101 rows
- Rebuild is idempotent: running it twice produces the same store
notes: Measured 102, not 101 — plants.csv gained Silphium albiflorum (ad12d5e) since the doc's 2026-09-18 count. Union derivation is by exact botanical_name string (not species-concept), matching the doc's own measurement.
close_reason: Schema, rebuild harness, and the plantable set built and tested

title: Plant data acquisition: build the claim store, pipeline, and export
description:
Build what nl-41o designed. That epic was analysis-and-planning only; its thirteen closed children produced docs/data-acquisition/01-11, which state themselves to be 'the schema/algorithm the implementation epic builds against'. This is that epic.

Scope: the SQLite claim store at data/claims.db (gitignored, rebuildable), the ingestion paths that fill it (USDA, the NCTX flora, NPIN), the per-field precedence rule and manual-corrections file that arbitrate it, the plants.csv export generated from it, the claims_* MCP introspection surface over it, and the two human-facing views 07 section 5 names.

Out of scope: reopening any nl-41o decision. Every child points at the doc section it implements rather than restating it — the docs are canonical and a second copy in bead prose would rot.
design:

title: PLANTS spine REPLACES the hex map as the homepage lead
description:
AUTHORITATIVE WORDING, revised by the owner 2026-09-16. Supersedes the earlier draft and closed issue nl-3hi.9.

 P - Plant natives that fit your site
 L - Leave the leaves, stems, and seed heads
 A - Avoid pesticides
 N - No invasives
 T - Trees first, especially native oaks
 S - Something blooming or fruiting every season

PROVENANCE: Claude-generated, not a published framework. It has no citation AS A MNEMONIC and must not be presented as 'from the research'. Label it a packaging of the literature - a memory aid - and cite each letter individually. An untested acronym also has no validation as a behaviour-change tool; stay humble given the finding that information alone rarely shifts yard behaviour.

WHAT THE REVISION FIXED:
 - P dropped 'mostly (aim for about 70% of plant mass)'. That number was the weakest item in the evidence audit and the same unreplicated Narango figure that sank the parcel map; 'plant mass' was also not homeowner-assessable and rewarded woody over herbaceous. Gone from the front page - it belongs on the reasoning page as provenance only. P now also absorbs HORTICULTURAL FIT (do not waste water on species that do not match the site).
 - L now names stems and seed heads explicitly, so it covers cavity/stem-nesting bees and winter seed as well as leaf litter. Statutory backing: Tex. Prop. Code 202.007(a)(1) protects composting vegetation and leaving grass clippings - an HOA cannot ban this outright.
 - S changed from 'Save birds: keep cats indoors and mark windows' to seasonal continuity, which gives bloomSuccession.js and birdFood.js a letter for the first time.

MAPPING TO THE EXISTING RULES ENGINE (4 of 6 letters now map, vs 2 before):
 P -> siteMatch.js + keystoneGenera.js + larvalHosts.js
 L -> no rule (management)
 A -> no rule (management)
 N -> dfw-avoid-non-natives.csv exists but is surfaced NOWHERE; no rule
 T -> verticalLayers.js + keystoneGenera.js
 S -> bloomSuccession.js + birdFood.js
Only L and A are pure behaviour with nothing computable behind them.

DEMOTED, NOT DELETED: cats indoors + marked windows left the mnemonic. They remain the BEST-EVIDENCED content available (Loss, Will & Marra 2013, Nature Communications 4:1396 - 1.3-4.0 billion US birds/yr, likely the single greatest anthropogenic source; Loss, Loss, Will & Marra 2014, The Condor 116(1) - 365-988 million/yr from building collisions, 44% at residences 1-3 stories). Owner confirmed earlier they want this on the site. Keep it as a companion surface beside L and A - things you DO rather than things you PLANT - and do not bury it. Carry the honesty notes: state the per-yard rate alongside the national aggregate, and say plainly that one indoor-kept cat outweighs one marked window.

N is not a stub. Leaving this note rather than editing the close reason so the history stays honest.

title: Pivot: from scoring parcels to surfacing what's needed and what's nearby
description:
SUPERSEDES the earlier plan recorded here (three interactive taxon hex layers + a graded/binary parcel-goodness map). Retired 2026-09-16 at the owner's direction; the reasoning below is why, and is worth keeping.

WHY THE PARCEL-GOODNESS MAP IS CUT. It stacked three unvalidated layers:
 1. the 70% native-biomass threshold - single-site, single-species, unreplicated (Narango, Tallamy & Marra 2018, PNAS 115(45))
 2. the parcels -> biomass-fraction conversion - NO published mapping exists at all
 3. a habitat scoring rubric - the category of instrument that empirically FAILED field validation (Garfinkel et al. 2023, Ecological Indicators 148:110062: 'the pollinator habitat score was not a significant predictor of bee and lepidopteran pollinator biodiversity')
And its output was actionable by nobody: no individual controls a hex. Most speculative thing on the site AND the least useful.

WHAT REPLACES IT - observational, not modelled:
 - habitat ANCHORS (creeks, parks, preserves, remnant prairie, cemeteries, utility easements) and distance to them = facts
 - what is already NEARBY = already built (iNaturalist, ecology/nearby-fauna.csv, ecosystem drawer)
 - what is MISSING in your yard = derived from plants.csv (growth_shape, height_ft, flowering_season_months give layer occupancy + bloom continuity)
 - what to PLANT = Part Two's FNCT-cited screen, the strongest asset on the site
 - PLANTS mnemonic as the prioritisation spine (see child issue)

HARD BOUNDARY: do NOT emit a connectivity score, gradient, or weighted lines. Anchor location and distance are facts; 'how connected you are' is a model, and scoring it rebuilds the parcel map with new geometry and none of the epistemic gain. Show distance and NAME what lies between (road, highway, continuous turf). Stop there.

STILL VALID from the earlier plan:
 - DECISION 0 = (B): index.html goes homeowner-facing; the three asks move to the reasoning page.
 - DECISION 4: no exclusion anywhere. No 'wrong street'. (Page never did say it - verified in verdictText.)
 - DECISION 6: reasoning gets its own page + nav entry.
 - DECISION 5 = (b) then (c), filed separately and unaffected.
 - The ADJACENCY TAXONOMY survives as EXPLANATION on the reasoning page, not as interactive geometry: birds = adjacency as DENSITY (fraction of a ~1-2ha window); bees = CO-LOCATION (forage + nesting substrate + bloom continuity within ~150m); herps = TOPOLOGY (unbroken passable path; fences and roads are hard barriers). Bee citations: Hofmann, Fleischmann & Renner 2020 (J. Hym. Res., 6-15mm bees, mean female flight 73-121m); Greenleaf et al. 2007 (Oecologia 153:589-596, range scales with body size). The urban literature is SPLIT (local-dominates: PLOS One 2024, Landscape Ecology 2025; isolation-matters: PubMed 40947939) - the reconciliation that the suburban matrix saturates the forage term is MY judgement call, not any paper's, and must be labelled as such per the repo's own convention.
 - Lepidoptera deliberately not a separate layer: Part Two IS the lep layer.

DEAD: three interactive hex views; any per-parcel score.

title: Name reconciliation is a prerequisite for every book-sourced field
description:
MEASURED on nl-41o.3: 119 of 469 rows in blackland-prairie-natives.csv matched no
treatment in the NCTX flora. The verified cause is 1999 NOMENCLATURE, not absence
-- Symphyotrichum oblongifolium is treated, as Aster oblongifolius.

Until a catalog name can be resolved to the name set a 1999 source uses, "not
found" is uninterpretable: it conflates renamed-since with genuinely-absent. That
makes it impossible to distinguish "the flora is silent, so native by convention"
from "we failed to look it up" -- and collapsing the two is exactly how
non-natives get silently promoted into recommendations.

USDA PLANTS publishes synonyms (field 17 in doc 01) and is the obvious source.
Sized as its own bead because it gates the flora, gates any future book source,
and is not specific to either.

Also measured: a binomial-only match misses infraspecific taxa entirely
(Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica read as absent though it is treated), and
this repo's catalogs are full of var./subsp. names -- Malvaviscus arboreus var.
drummondii, Achillea millefolium var. occidentalis, Anisacanthus quadrifidus var.
wrightii. Reconciliation has to handle rank, not just the binomial.

See docs/data-acquisition/03-document-corpus.md §5.

title: Working source-probe MCP tools, for use during the analysis
description:
Build phase 1 of the introspection surface (nl-41o.8) as a REAL, USABLE tool,
early, so the investigation beads are done with instruments rather than by hand.

This is the one IMPLEMENTATION bead in an otherwise analysis-only epic, and it
is deliberate. nl-41o.1 has to answer "does any source publish this field at
county granularity" for dozens of fields, and nl-41o.2 has to verify coverage
and access claims across a dozen sources. Doing that by reading documentation
produces beliefs; doing it with a probe produces measurements. The tool pays for
itself inside the epic that specifies it.

Scope is deliberately small: probe a source, show what came back, report which
required fields it populated. No claim store, no writes, no persistence beyond
a cache. Everything else waits for nl-41o.8 and nl-41o.4.
design:
BUILD ONLY PHASE 1 from nl-41o.8: source probe, field sniff, run state.
Resist the rest — coverage and provenance need the claim store and building
them against a guess at the model will have to be redone.

STARTING POINT: the usda-plants MCP server already exists and is wired into the
session (usda_search_by_location, usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
usda_download_plant_list). Decide whether this extends it or sits beside it;
nl-41o.8 flags that two servers with overlapping vocabulary is the bad outcome.

WHAT MAKES IT USEFUL RATHER THAN A DETOUR:
  - RAW output, not a normalized view. The whole point is seeing what the source
    actually said, so a parse bug is distinguishable from a source gap. The Alnus
    case from nl-jsm.1 is the precedent: a clean-looking extraction silently
    dropped a row and only a second view of the same document caught it.
  - Cache responses. The availability audit will probe the same species
    repeatedly across several sittings, and re-fetching is slow and rude to the
    source.
  - Report per-field population against the required-fields list from nl-41o.1,
    once that list exists. Before it exists, probe against the fields already
    known missing: county nativity, soil/light/water tolerance, mature width,
    commercial availability.

NOT IN SCOPE: writing anything into plants.csv or any claim store. This tool
reads and reports. Collection is a later epic.
acceptance_criteria:
• Probe returns a source's RAW response for a species, without normalizing it
• Reports which of the target fields that source populated for that species
• Responses cached, so a repeated probe does not re-fetch
• Extends or sits beside the existing usda-plants server, with the choice
  recorded and no overlapping tool vocabulary
• Read-only: no path from this tool to a committed data file
notes:
NOT a gate on nl-41o.1/.2 — deliberately. Those two and this one INTERLEAVE: .1 names a required field, this probes whether a source publishes it, the answer sharpens .1's availability audit, repeat. A hard dependency either way would be wrong, since this bead's own design consumes .1's field list while .1's availability half consumes this bead's output. Start with the fields already known missing (county nativity, soil/light/water tolerance, mature width, commercial availability) and let the list grow.
TOOLING (decided on the epic 2026-08-27): built in NODE, extending tools/usda-plants
rather than sitting beside it — that settles this bead's open question about extend
vs adjacent, and satisfies nl-41o.8's one-vocabulary rule. Cache backed by SQLite
(node:sqlite, built in — no dependency).
PROBE TARGETS, ordered by cost-of-being-wrong (from nl-41o.1):
1. BONAP — county nativity, and on what terms. The one unresolved blocker.
2. The distribution endpoint AT SCALE. nl-41o.1 measured 4 species; confirm it holds for
   several hundred and establish a polite rate. One POST per species = ~500 requests for
   the Blackland list. Endpoint:
   POST /api/PlantProfile/getDownloadDistributionDocumentation {"masterId": <id>}
3. LBJ NPIN — regional bloom/fruit timing and mature width (the non-book candidate for
   the width gap).
4. The other 55 USDA characteristics — nl-41o.1 sampled ONE species (Quercus shumardii).
   Confirm the useful ones are populated broadly, not just for a well-studied oak.
CAUTION to carry into any new source: mapCharacteristics.js:96-113 documents that USDA's
live Shade Tolerance values run OPPOSITE to its own Swagger enum (verified 14/15 vs 0/15).
That inversion already caused commit ed9d75c. Check any light field the same way before
trusting it.
PROBE TARGETS REVISED after nl-41o.2. BONAP is DONE — do not spend probe effort there;
its terms answer the question and the blocker is legal, not technical.
New ordering:
1. /api/characteristicSearchResults and /api/characteristicSearchResultsDownload — a
   DIFFERENT bulk path from the plants-search-results one known to time out. If either
   works it replaces per-species fetching wholesale. Cheapest high-upside probe available.
2. NPIN AT VOLUME — does per-species retrieval hold beyond three pages, and at what rate?
   Measured working with a browser UA on CHLI2/QUSH/ILVO. Pair with an EMAIL to the Center,
   since the terms page is the one thing Cloudflare blocks. Do not work around it.
3. NPIN larval-host and light-set COVERAGE — found on 2 of 2 species examined. If broadly
   populated, these are the fields that un-stick R5 and R8's light check.
4. GBIF county filtering via GADM — a licence-tagged second opinion on county presence.
5. /api/PlantWildlife fill rate (carried over from nl-41o.1).

Field sniff is honest by construction: near-miss key matches (measured live: 'Seed Spread Rate' matches a width regex on Quercus shumardii) are surfaced as a diagnostic for human review, never auto-adopted as a value; characteristicsCount distinguishes a zero-record taxon from a real per-field gap.

title: MCP interface for pipeline introspection
description:
Design the MCP surface an agent uses to watch and steer the collection as it
runs — not just to read the finished data.

The existing usda-plants MCP tools fetch. That is enough to pull a record and
not enough to answer "why does this species have no soil tolerance", "what did
this source actually return for it", "which claim won this field and what lost",
or "what is left to collect". Without those, every diagnosis means re-running
the pipeline by hand and reading its output, which is slow and does not compose.

Design only. The tools this names are built with the pipeline, not before it.
design:
PHASED DELIBERATELY, because most of this needs no data model and waiting for
one would keep the tooling away from exactly the work it makes faster. Only the
claim-store queries depend on nl-41o.4; everything else can be designed and used
before it exists. See nl-41o.9, which builds the first phase as a working tool
to be used DURING the investigation beads.

PHASE 1 — needs nothing but a source. Usable while doing nl-41o.1/.2/.3.
  Source probe   What a given source returns for a given species, RAW, without
                 committing it. The way to tell a bad parse from a bad source
                 without polluting anything. This is also how the availability
                 audit in nl-41o.1 gets answered per field rather than assumed,
                 and how the licensing/coverage claims in nl-41o.2 get checked
                 rather than taken from documentation.
  Field sniff    For one species, which of the required fields does this source
                 actually populate? Turns "USDA has soil tolerance" from a
                 belief into a measurement.
  Run state      What is queued, in flight, failed, rate-limited; what a retry
                 would do.

PHASE 2 — needs the claim store from nl-41o.4.
  Coverage       What is missing, sliced by species / field / source. Both the
                 quality report and the work queue; one query serving both is
                 the point.
  Provenance     For one species x field: every claim, its source, retrieval
                 time, confidence, which won and WHY. The 'why' matters — a
                 precedence rule that cannot be explained cannot be debugged.
  Conflicts      Unadjudicated disagreements, plus a path to record a correction
                 through the same interface. Per nl-41o.5 a correction needs a
                 reason and an author, so the tool must demand both.
  Dry run        What a collection pass WOULD change, before it changes it.

DESIGN NOTES:
  - Read tools and write tools are different risk classes. A correction is a
    write and should look like one.
  - Return shapes small and composable. codegraph_explore is the good local
    model: one call answers the whole question instead of a dozen round trips.
  - Introspection must not require the pipeline to be running.
  - Some of this deserves a human-facing view in the app, not only an agent tool.

CHECK FIRST what the existing usda-plants MCP server already offers
(usda_search_by_location, usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
usda_download_plant_list) and whether it is extended or joined by a second
server. Two servers with overlapping vocabulary would be worse than one.
acceptance_criteria:
• A named tool per capability area, with arguments and return shape
• Read and write tools clearly separated, corrections requiring reason + author
• A decision on extending the existing usda-plants server vs adding one
• A note on which introspection deserves a human-facing view, not just a tool
close_reason: Delivered docs/data-acquisition/07-mcp-introspection.md: cataloged the two Phase 1 tools nl-41o.9 already built (usda_probe, usda_probe_target_fields), specified six Phase 2 tools (claims_coverage, claims_provenance, claims_conflicts, claims_sources, claims_correct, claims_dry_run) covering all six lookups named in nl-41o.4/nl-41o.6, and deferred run_state as having no real process yet to introspect. Read/write separated (claims_correct is the sole write tool, reason+author required); claims_coverage and claims_conflicts flagged for a human-facing view; server stays named usda-plants, reasoned explicitly.

title: Data model: species identity, claims, and provenance
description:
Design the model the collected data lands in, and the indexing that serves it.

Two hard parts:

IDENTITY. Which rows are the same plant? Synonyms are not an edge case here —
Packera obovata / Senecio obovatus already broke a rule in the shipped epic and
needed a synonym_of column to fix. Varieties (Cercis canadensis var. texensis),
cultivars ('Oklahoma', 'Nana', 'Undaunted'), and hybrids all need a position.

CLAIMS. A field is not a value, it is a value ASSERTED BY A SOURCE. Two sources
disagreeing is normal and must be representable without one silently
overwriting the other. That shape is what makes provenance, confidence,
conflict resolution, and quality metrics possible at all — get it wrong and
every one of those becomes impossible downstream.
design:
IDENTITY — what already bites:
  - Packera obovata vs Senecio obovatus: handled today by a synonym_of column in
    ecology/host-genera.csv. Works for one genus; will not scale.
  - Cultivars: "Ilex vomitoria 'Nana'" and "Muhlenbergia reverchonii 'Undaunted'"
    are in plants.csv and in both layouts. No botanical database indexes them.
    A cultivar inherits most of its species' data and overrides some (mature
    size, most obviously — 'Nana' is 4 ft against the species' 18 ft). Decide
    whether that is inheritance, a separate row, or both.
  - Varieties: "Cercis canadensis var. texensis" — an earlier commit (e2a2391)
    already had to prefer the nominate record over unlisted varieties.

CLAIMS — the shape to settle:
  something like { species_id, field, value, source, retrieved_at, confidence }
  with the flat CSV the app reads being a DERIVED PROJECTION of the claim store,
  not the store itself. That separation is what lets a re-crawl update sources
  without destroying manual corrections.

  Decide: does the app keep reading a flat plants.csv (simple, git-diffable, and
  what every existing loader expects), with the claim store behind it? Changing
  what the app reads touches src/data/plantParser.js and everything downstream,
  so there is a real argument for keeping the projection.

INDEXING: what lookups must be fast — by species, by field, by source, by
county, by "which species have no sourced value for X" (that last one drives the
quality metrics and the work queue, so it is not optional).

CONSTRAINT: whatever is chosen must stay reviewable in a pull request. Part of
why the current CSVs work is that a human can read the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
• An identity scheme covering synonyms, varieties, and cultivars, with the
