title: Export bundle loops over views[]
description:
captureViewToPng (src/export/viewCapture.js) is per-SVG and needs no change, but its caller at src/app.js:317 enumerates the three panels by hand ({ view: project.plan, svg: svgRefs.topSvg, fileName: 'plan-view.png' }, ...). Move that loop to views[].

Crop views ARE included in the export — a detail callout is exactly the kind of thing worth having as a PNG. File names come from the view id: plan-view.png, shade-bed-view.png, east-view.png.
acceptance_criteria: Exporting a project with four views yields four PNGs named from view ids, each with its background composited. Existing three-view export output is unchanged apart from any id-derived renaming.
notes: Partly done already: nl-tz7.4 replaced the hand-enumerated export panel list with a loop over the cloned viewPanels, so crop views are included automatically. That also renamed the files — elevations went from <id>-elevation.png to <id>-view.png, matching the plan doc's plan-view.png / shade-bed-view.png scheme. What remains here is whatever naming or per-view export options this bead still wants on top.
close_reason: New src/render/backgroundCrop.js resolves a view's background image and, for a backgroundFrom detail view, the patch of it to show. Consumed twice: viewConfig.js sets background-size/-position on the panel (and clears both when a view stops borrowing, since panels are reused by id), and app.js passes the same rect to captureViewToPng as a sourceRect so the exported PNG shows the same patch instead of the whole photo stretched. The crop is derived by mapping the detail's corners through the SOURCE view's transform, which handles mirrored elevations and the plan y-flip for free. normalizeProjectConfig now rejects backgroundFrom across differing type/viewFrom, and the Setup panel only offers compatible sources. tests/backgroundCrop.test.js covers the worked example, the equal-extent and full-width guards, and both mirrored and unmirrored elevations. Export loop over views[] was already in place from nl-tz7.4; crop backgrounds were the missing piece.

title: Two-point ruler calibration from the background photo (optional)
description:
OPTIONAL — the user asked to explore photo calibration without committing to it. Ship the rest of the epic first; this is a recommendation because it is unusually cheap, not a requirement. Dropping it leaves the numeric extentFt field doing the same job.

Three gestures cover the whole of 'calibrate against a photo', with no homography, no new data model, and no OpenSeadragon:
  - drag across a known length in the photo, type the real length -> solves pxPerFt, hence extentFt
  - click the ground line -> originFt.y   (covered by nl-tz7.7)
  - click the near edge   -> originFt.x   (covered by nl-tz7.7)

This bead is the ruler only. styles.css:876 is background-size: 100% 100%, so viewBox units map proportionally onto the image and the measurement is well-posed.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the ruler across a fence panel of known length and entering that length updates extentFt, and the view re-scales so the plan matches the photo. Unit-tested math for the solve.
close_reason: Two-point ruler shipped. resolveRulerCalibration + measureRuler in src/render/setupOverlay.js solve extentFt from a drag across the background photo and a typed real length; setupController gains setRuler()/onRuler (the armed pointer measures instead of moving handles); setupPanel gains the Measure a known length toggle, the px/ft readout, and the length field; app.js holds the segment in appState.ruler and clears it before the rebuild. Unit tests cover the solve on a plan and on a mirrored (north) elevation — asserting the near edge and ground line keep their fraction of the photo — plus diagonal equivalence and the misclick/nonsense-length guards. One e2e spec measures half the plan panel and asserts Width (ft) doubles the typed length. Two bugs found by that spec and fixed: the pointer's last position is now held outside the rAF-throttled payload (a release after a flushed frame measured zero), and the panel only learns the measurement on drag end (growing it mid-gesture shifted the canvas under the pointer). AGENTS.md documents the gesture and the anchoring rule.

title: Mobile polish: tap targets, resize thrash, numeric scale input
description:
Smaller items from the mobile review.

- Tap targets below the 44px guideline: chips 31px tall, #projectSelect 29px, .view-panel__toggle ~24px. Pill switches at 46px are fine.
- window.addEventListener('resize', render) (src/app.js:520): Android's address bar showing/hiding and the keyboard opening on #scaleInput both fire resize, causing a full re-render of 192 plant groups x 3 views mid-scroll. Debounce it, or compare dimensions before re-rendering.
- #scaleInput is type='number' with step='0.01' - opens a numeric keypad and is fiddly on touch. On mobile the slider alone (plus the per-view '1 ft = N px' badge) is enough.

NOT a problem, checked and confirmed fine: the drag hitbox. MIN_HITBOX_RADIUS_PX = 28 (dragController.js:3) is multiplied by scaleFactor = viewBox / rect (:362, :418), so it is 28 SCREEN px regardless of render size. No small-screen inversion; a 56px-diameter target is acceptable.
close_reason: Tap targets (chips, view-panel__toggle, projectSelect) bumped to 44px min-height on phone (<=600px). Resize handler debounced 150ms and skips re-render when innerWidth is unchanged, so address-bar show/hide and keyboard-open no longer force a full 192-group x3-view re-render. #scaleInput (numeric keypad) hidden on phone; slider + per-view badge remain. Verified in-browser at 412px.

title: Layout history seeds bypass parsePlantLayoutCsv validation
description: appState.plants can come from layoutHistoryInstance.getCurrentPlants() (src/app.js), which is seeded from the server's layout-history.json. Those entries are plain plant arrays and never pass through parsePlantLayoutCsv, so the duplicate-id constraint added in nl-92d does not cover them. Not reachable today: cloning routes through buildCloneId, CSV load now throws, and a scan of projects/example-frontyard/layout-history.json (6 entries) found no duplicates. Worth closing if a future path writes history directly.
acceptance_criteria: Either history seeds are validated on load, or a note records why the path is safe by construction.
close_reason: Not worth pursuing; path is safe by construction (no known way to write history without going through validated CSV load/clone flow)

title: Duplicate plant id in backyard planting_layout.csv
description: projects/backyard/planting_layout.csv has two rows sharing the id 'four-nerve-daisy-front' (lines 26 and 27). Ids are used to look up plants for dragging, cloning, and hover/target highlighting, so the second row is effectively unreachable — dragging either silhouette moves the first match. Pre-existing, found while verifying the multi-project change; not caused by it.
acceptance_criteria: Every id in planting_layout.csv is unique; consider validating uniqueness in parsePlantLayoutCsv.
close_reason: Duplicates already removed by nl-y8y; parsePlantLayoutCsv now throws on repeated ids, with unit tests.

title: FUTURE: agentic system to compile catalog data for plants users request
description: New users will want plants that aren't among the 63 in the catalog. Owner direction 2026-09-23: rather than letting users type in their own attributes, build an agentic pipeline that compiles sourced data for a requested plant into the claim store (with sources, licences and review status, per docs/data-acquisition/), and a human approves it before it reaches plants.csv. Tabled for now.

title: FUTURE: site conditions per area of the yard
description: project.site is one {sun, water, soil} for the whole yard, but real yards have shade under a tree, a wet low spot, a hot strip by the driveway, so the rules engine can only check a plant against the yard-wide average. Idea: a feature such as a bed can carry its own site, using SITE_VOCABULARY; a plant uses the conditions of the area it's in, falling back to the yard's; anything nobody declared is still reported as undeclared. Owner decision 2026-09-23: consider this after the multi-user work and the other model changes are built.

title: FUTURE: public yard views with owner-controlled privacy
description: The owner wants yards to be shareable publicly, with the owner choosing what is exposed. Example: expose only the plant list, while keeping the photos, layout geometry and location private. Build it on the visibility field added by nl-3s5.4. Every exposed field is an explicit opt-in, and location is never exposed beyond the coarse place label. Deferred until multi-user ships.
